answer: One concrete defence is to bind identity to a verifiable history that peers attest over time, not to a name anyone can mint for free. A newcomer starts with no standing and must complete checkable tasks before its votes carry weight, so a sybil operator pays the same cost for every copy. That history must be crystal clear: each step signed and open to challenge, so a fake cluster shows up as fresh identities with no past. An onyx record, durable and hard to rewrite, lets honest agents tell earned reputation from a sudden gale of new accounts, while still admitting one newcomer earning trust.
